confirm.stopDesc: Deletes the CR (cascading to reclaim the Pods) to release compute. The config is kept, so you can clone it to rebuild the service.
confirm.deleteDescList: This also deletes the LWS and gateway resources and all Pods.
confirm.deleteDescDetail: This also deletes the LWS and gateway resources and all Pods.

messages.stopped: llm-d inference service stopped (the config is kept; clone it to rebuild)

basic.displayNameTooltip: Also used as the prefix of the K8s task name, so it must be a valid DNS name: start with a lowercase letter, be 3-20 characters long, contain only a-z, 0-9 and '-', and end with a letter or digit. For notes in other languages such as Chinese, use the "Description" field below. The final task name = this name + '-' + 10 random characters, generated by the backend at creation. Multi-node inference names are 9 characters shorter than training and inference names, because Kueue embeds the task name in a length-limited label.
basic.displayNameAscii: Chinese and full-width characters are not allowed. Put any notes in the "Description" field below.
basic.displayNamePattern: Must start with a lowercase letter, contain only a-z, 0-9 and '-', and end with a letter or digit.
basic.descriptionTooltip: A short description (optional), to help you recognize it in the list and details.
basic.descriptionPlaceholder: e.g. DeepSeek-V3 multi-node TP/EP inference (LWS + sgl-gateway)

gateway.instanceTypeTooltip: The gateway is a CPU-only router, so it can use its own instance type (the CPU pool is the cheapest option; it can also share the worker's GPU instance). The backend checks that the instance type is within your quota.
gateway.instanceTypePlaceholder: Select an instance type (CPU or GPU)
gateway.instanceTypePlaceholderEmpty: No assigned instance types (contact an admin to set up a quota)
gateway.instanceTypeNotFound: No instance types in this Workspace
gateway.templateTooltip: The gateway is a CPU-only routing layer and uses no GPUs. CPU and memory are governed by CPU pool templates maintained by admins.
gateway.templatePlaceholder: Select a CPU pool resource template (maintained by admins)
gateway.specTooltip: CPU and memory are governed by the CPU pool resource template; switching templates syncs them automatically. Request = limit.
gateway.noTemplates: No CPU pool resource templates yet · ask a Workspace admin to create one in Admin Console → Resource Template
gateway.replicasTooltip: Number of sgl-model-gateway replicas (stateless routing; multiple replicas give high availability).
gateway.exposeAlbTooltip: If on, an internal ALB is created for this instance, giving you an HTTP endpoint you can call directly. If off, the service is reachable only from inside the cluster (you can test it through the platform proxy on the details page). This is set at creation; to change it later you must delete and recreate the service.
gateway.extraArgsTooltip: Append or override sgl-model-gateway router tuning arguments (appended at the end; for duplicate names the later one wins). Leave empty to use the official defaults. One argument per line.
gateway.extraArgsExtra: One argument per line, e.g. --cache-threshold=0.5; leave empty to use the official defaults (cache_aware, queue, health-check, etc.)

image.help: Choose from the images under "Asset Management → Image" whose purpose includes inference, or type any full image URI (including the tag). The llm-d worker runs the SGLang inference engine, so the standard lmsysorg/sglang image is enough. Private ECR is only supported in the AWS account and Region this platform runs in.
image.label: SGLang image (full name, including tag)
image.empty: If the Image Hub has no images, you can use the default lmsysorg/sglang image directly, or register a custom image under <registry>"Asset Management → Image"</registry>.
image.hint: The dropdown lists images under "Image" whose purpose includes inference; you can also type any image URI.
image.required: Select or enter an image URI.

model.fsxTooltip: Choose an authorized FSx file system (select one). It is mounted at /fsx in the container; enter the absolute model path below. If no resources are listed, contact an admin to grant access.
model.fsxNone: You have no authorized FSx in this Workspace · contact an admin
model.fsxHint: FSx is mounted at /fsx; write the model path as /fsx/<model-dir>
model.fsxPlaceholder: Select an FSx mount source (select one)
model.fsxNotFound: No authorized FSx in this Workspace
model.modelDiskHint: The model disk is mounted at /model in the container. In the "Launch configuration" script, write: --model-path /model/<model-dir>
model.s3Tooltip: Choose a bucket the Workspace is authorized for (S3 already mounted). The backend creates a dedicated mount, with the prefix pointing at the model directory.
model.s3Placeholder: Select a bucket (must be authorized for the Workspace)
model.s3PlaceholderEmpty: No authorized S3 in this Workspace (contact an admin)
model.s3NotFound: No authorized S3 in this Workspace
model.s3PrefixTooltip: The prefix of the model within the bucket (pointing at the model directory). The mount root is the model itself, and sglang reads /model directly.
model.s3PrefixExtra: e.g. models/qwen2.5-0.5b (the mount root is this directory)

resource.instanceTypeTooltip: The worker and gateway use the same instance type (GPU pool). The gateway uses no GPUs, so placing it on a GPU instance does not consume quota. The backend checks that the instance type is within your quota.
resource.instanceTypePlaceholder: Select an instance type in the GPU pool
resource.instanceTypePlaceholderEmpty: No assigned GPU instance types (contact an admin to set up a quota)
resource.instanceTypeNotFound: No GPU instance types in this Workspace
resource.templateTooltip: Per-node GPU, CPU, memory and EFA of a worker are governed by templates maintained by admins. Total = replicas × nodes × template.
resource.templatePlaceholder: Select a resource template (maintained by admins)
resource.noTemplates: No resource templates yet · ask a Workspace admin to create one in Admin Console → Resource Template
resource.replicasTooltip: Number of independent leader + worker groups (LWS replicas), for data parallelism. Total GPUs = replicas × nodes × GPUs per Pod.
resource.nodesTooltip: How many nodes one inference instance spans for TP/EP (LWS size). ★ Minimum 2: this is a multi-node gang, and size=1 triggers a Kueue division by zero (bug#6486).
resource.perNodeSpecTooltip: GPU, CPU, memory and EFA are governed by the resource template (locked to a single worker node); switching templates syncs them automatically.
resource.quotaOver: · over quota; it will wait for quota after you submit
resource.quotaCollecting_one: · {{count}} GPU in total · remaining quota is being collected
resource.quotaCollecting_other: · {{count}} GPUs in total · remaining quota is being collected

launch.heading: Launch script (SGLang)
launch.help:
The whole script runs via /bin/sh -c (the backend renders command=["/bin/sh","-c"], args=[script]).
--model-path: FSx is mounted at the same path as in your dev instance, so use the full absolute path (e.g. /fsx/team-a-data/models/qwen2.5-0.5b); S3 is mounted at /model, so use /model/.
Edit the multi-node tensor/expert parallelism flags --tp-size / --ep-size directly here.
The LWS networking placeholders $LWS_LEADER_ADDRESS / $LWS_GROUP_SIZE / $LWS_WORKER_INDEX are pre-filled; do not delete them.
launch.scriptExtra: The sglang.launch_server launch command is pre-filled; edit --model-path / --tp-size / --ep-size as needed
